title: Atomic pristine recovery-binding install
description: Objective: provide the store primitive required for safe genesis recovery identity installation without changing the existing restore replacement API. Deliverable: add an atomic project-scoped install-if-pristine operation that, under one SQLite write transaction, requires ACTIVE and PENDING to be absent and the authoritative store to have no disqualifying business/recovery history, inserts a validated binding without DELETE/replace, and returns either the committed record, the exact valid current winner, or a stable refusal tuple. This is a prerequisite for task-e19074f841f9450296799abfba9bfcaa; current installRecoveryBinding is intentionally replacement semantics and two concurrent absent readers can overwrite each other. NOT in scope: daemon crypto/minting, restore-controller behavior, session authentication, schema changes, or changing installRecoveryBinding replacement semantics. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: A public SqliteEventStore initial-install method validates the recovery-binding codec and atomically requires a project-scoped pristine state plus both recovery slots absent before INSERT; it never deletes or overwrites an existing binding.

Two file-backed handles racing distinct valid bindings produce exactly one committed binding and one coherent current-winner/refusal result; both read the same ACTIVE refs after reopen, and the generated race executes at least once.

A concurrent/pre-existing ACTIVE restore binding, any PENDING binding, ordinary authoritative decision/event history, malformed row, or unprovable transaction outcome grants no genesis authority and returns an exact stable code and layer.
The existing installRecoveryBinding replacement and rollback semantics, recovery-anchor installer behavior, and public read surface remain unchanged with their existing exact tests green.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not change installRecoveryBinding replacement semantics; genesis consumes a separate narrowly named initial-install capability.
The pristine check and insert must share one SQLite write transaction; no read-then-write sequence or caller-asserted pristine flag.
Failure tests assert exact reason code and store layer, generated race tables assert nonzero execution, and a mutation back to DELETE/replace must redden the race/restore-preservation test.
Keep production sources focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; preserve foreign work and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Land the capability vocabulary in a NEW file packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install.ts (plus its one-line ESM bridge recovery-initial-install.js: `export * from "./recovery-initial-install.ts";`, matching every sibling production module). Define its OWN closed registry — do NOT extend RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES: packages/store/src/recovery-install-entrypoint.test.ts:33 asserts `reasonCodeCount: 8` inside a whole-object toEqual, so growing the shared registry reddens an existing test the DoD requires to stay green. Publish: `RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_REASON_CODES = Object.freeze(["RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_SLOT_UNSUPPORTED", "RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_PENDING_PRESENT", "RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT", "RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_ALREADY_BOUND"] as const)` + its type; three FROZEN MODULE-CONSTANT refusals (same 7-field shape as RecoveryInstallRefused — ok:false, outcome:"REFUSED", authority:"NONE", truth:"UNKNOWN", code, layer, reason — nothing observed at the failure site may reach them) for the first three codes, all at RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER; and the result union `RecoveryInitialInstallResult = RecoveryInstallCommitted | RecoveryInitialInstallCurrent | RecoveryInstallRefused | RecoveryInitialInstallRefused`. RecoveryInstallCommitted is REUSED unchanged so a committed genesis record is byte-for-byte the same shape as a replacement install. RecoveryInitialInstallCurrent is a NEW ok:true observation, not a refusal: `{ ok: true, outcome: "CURRENT", authority: "NONE", code: "RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_ALREADY_BOUND", layer: typeof RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER, binding: RecoveryBindingRecord, bindingDigest: string }` — it carries the exact valid current winner AND a stable code+layer, so the caller can neither mistake it for an install (outcome !== "INSTALLED", authority NONE) nor be left without a stable identifier. Reuse the existing two layers verbatim; do NOT add a third — recovery-install.test.ts:77 asserts RECOVERY_INSTALL_LAYERS toEqual exactly two.

Write the failing refusal-surface tests in a NEW file packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install.test.ts, following recovery-install.test.ts conventions (mkdtempSync temp dirs pushed onto a module array, afterEach rmSync, every store opened and closed inside the `it` body with try/finally — never in a describe body; a held SQLite handle makes the Windows afterEach rmSync throw EPERM and kills the vitest worker with zero test output). Cases, each asserting BOTH the exact code and the exact layer: (a) registry closure — RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_REASON_CODES has 4 entries, is unique, and is DISJOINT from RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES (no code can be ambiguous between the two surfaces); (b) unscoped handle via SqliteEventStore.open(...) with both a well-formed AND a malformed binding -> RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED / RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER, proving scope is asked before the codec; (c) codec refusals on a scoped handle (extra key -> RECOVERY_BINDING_SHAPE_INVALID, bad codec version -> RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED) at RECOVERY_BINDING_CODEC_LAYER; (d) a valid binding naming slot PENDING -> RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_SLOT_UNSUPPORTED / TRANSACTION layer, and ACTIVE stays ABSENT; (e) a store holding only a PENDING binding (installed through the existing installRecoveryBinding) -> RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_PENDING_PRESENT, and a store holding BOTH a PENDING and a valid ACTIVE -> still PENDING_PRESENT (pins which guard answers first); (f) closed handle -> throws DurableStoreError with code STORE_CLOSED, not a refusal. Expect this file NOT to compile yet — installInitialRecoveryBinding does not exist. Record that tsc error text as the RED evidence for the step.

Add the history, malformed-row, durability and restore-preservation tests to packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install.test.ts. HISTORY (hand-written table of exactly 2 fixtures, with `expect(historyFixtures.length).toBe(2)` and per-fixture pre-state row counts asserted BEFORE the install attempt so a fixture that silently generated nothing cannot pass): H1 commits one real decision through commitExpectedVersionDecision (one event carrying one outbox message) and asserts command_decisions/command_receipts/domain_events/aggregate_heads/outbox_messages all count > 0; H2 uses a raw `new DatabaseSync(path)` handle to insert ONE aggregate_heads row only (that table carries no foreign key, so it is the one history source reachable in isolation) and asserts heads count 1 with receipts/events/decisions counts 0. Both must return RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT / TRANSACTION layer, and ACTIVE must still read ABSENT afterwards. MALFORMED ACTIVE: after a replacement install, tamper binding_bytes only -> RECOVERY_BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH at CODEC layer; tamper the incarnation_ref COLUMN only (bytes and digest still agree) -> RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED at TRANSACTION layer; in both, the initial install must refuse rather than overwrite the unreadable row. DURABILITY: on a fresh file-backed project store, installInitialRecoveryBinding returns outcome INSTALLED with the caller's binding and digest; reopen and assert readRecoveryBinding("ACTIVE") is FOUND with the same incarnationRef, digest and payload bytes, and PENDING is ABSENT. RESTORE PRESERVATION (the mutation-drill anchor): install an ACTIVE binding through the EXISTING replacement installRecoveryBinding (this is the restore path), capture its digest, then call installInitialRecoveryBinding with a DIFFERENT valid binding — assert ok true, outcome "CURRENT", authority "NONE", code RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_ALREADY_BOUND, layer TRANSACTION, and that binding.incarnationRef/bindingDigest are the RESTORE's values, not the caller's; then reopen and assert the stored ACTIVE digest and payload are still byte-identical to the restore's.

Implement the transaction in packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install.ts as `export class RecoveryInitialInstallStore extends RecoveryInstallStore` with the single public method `installInitialRecoveryBinding(input: unknown): RecoveryInitialInstallResult`. Reuse, do not re-derive: in packages/store/src/recovery-install.ts widen `releaseInstallTransaction` from private to protected and export `SELECT_BINDING_SQL`, `INSERT_BINDING_SQL`, `rowMatchesBinding` and `isUniqueConstraintViolation` — no behavior change there, so its existing tests stay green and the two installers cannot drift on row validation or on unprovable-outcome handling. Exact order: requireOpen(); scope check (projectId === null || !writeProjectAsserted -> RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED) BEFORE the codec; encodeRecoveryBinding(input) and return its refusal as-is; slot !== "ACTIVE" -> RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_SLOT_UNSUPPORTED; then ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` covering everything that follows — assertDurableProjectBinding(); PENDING row present -> PENDING_PRESENT; history present -> HISTORY_PRESENT via a single statement of EXISTS legs over command_decisions (scoped `WHERE project_id = ?` with this.projectId), command_receipts, domain_events, aggregate_heads and outbox_messages; ACTIVE row present -> decode it with decodeRecoveryBinding (return the codec refusal on bad bytes), cross-check with rowMatchesBinding (return RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED), else return the CURRENT winner built from the DECODED bytes; otherwise run INSERT_BINDING_SQL ALONE — no DELETE, no INSERT OR REPLACE, no UPSERT — and COMMIT, returning INSTALLED. There is no read-then-write window and no caller-asserted pristine flag: every guard reads under the write lock the same transaction inserts in. A guard that refuses must ROLLBACK and return its refusal (a refusal is not a fault); route every thrown failure and any failing ROLLBACK through releaseInstallTransaction so an unprovable outcome poisons the handle and raises DurableStoreError OUTCOME_UNKNOWN rather than reporting a benign refusal, and map a UNIQUE violation to RECOVERY_INSTALL_INCARNATION_CONFLICT. Comment WHY the history legs are those five and why derived tables (projections, inbox_receipts, event_subscriptions, cursor_generations) and the bootstrap rows in store_metadata/store_project_binding are excluded. Keep the file under 250 physical lines (`grep -c '' <file>`); if it grows past that, split the vocabulary into recovery-initial-install-contracts.ts plus its .js bridge.

Publish the capability through the existing chain and turn steps 2-3 green. In packages/store/src/decision-ledger.ts: `class DecisionLedgerStore extends RecoveryInitialInstallStore` (the new class extends RecoveryInstallStore, so the chain order is preserved), add `installInitialRecoveryBinding` to the DecisionLedgerCore interface and to the frozen delegate object created by createDecisionLedgerCore. In packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts add the public passthrough `installInitialRecoveryBinding(input: unknown): RecoveryInitialInstallResult` next to installRecoveryBinding, with a one-line comment stating it INSERTS only into a pristine store and never replaces (measured: that file is 358 physical lines today and this adds ~8, staying under the 400 split bar; do not restructure it in this task). In packages/store/src/index.ts export RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_REASON_CODES as a runtime value plus the RecoveryInitialInstall* types. Then run `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test` and confirm every case from steps 2-3 is green and that recovery-install.test.ts, recovery-install-entrypoint.test.ts (its reasonCodeCount 8 assertion must be untouched and passing), recovery-anchor*.test.ts and store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts are unchanged and green.

Prove the concurrency claim with two file-backed handles. Add packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install-race-worker.mjs modelled on command-decision-race-worker.mjs: import { SqliteEventStore } from "./index.ts" (importing through the package ROOT also proves the method is a real runtime value and not a type-only export), post PREOPEN_READY, Atomics.wait on gate slot 0, openForProject, post READY, Atomics.wait on gate slot 1, call installInitialRecoveryBinding with the worker's own distinct valid binding, then CLOSE THE STORE IN A FINALLY BEFORE posting the RESULT (a still-open handle makes the test's rmSync fail with EPERM on Windows). The RESULT message carries kind, ok, outcome, code, layer, incarnationRef, bindingDigest and `initialInstallType: typeof SqliteEventStore.prototype.installInitialRecoveryBinding`. Add the two-phase gate/start/release harness inline in recovery-initial-install.test.ts (same shape as startDecisionRaceWorker/releaseDecisionRace) and assert: both workers returned a RESULT (results.length === 2 — the race actually executed, not zero cases); each result's initialInstallType is "function"; the sorted outcomes are exactly ["CURRENT", "INSTALLED"]; the CURRENT result's incarnationRef and bindingDigest equal the INSTALLED one's and its code/layer are RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_ALREADY_BOUND / RECOVERY_INSTALL_TRANSACTION_LAYER; the winning ref is one of the two proposed refs; and after reopening the file, ACTIVE reads FOUND with that same incarnationRef and digest while PENDING is ABSENT. Bound the wait — if a worker never reports, fail by name rather than hanging the suite.

Run the mutation drills that prove these tests are attached to the production surface. For EACH drill: record `sha256sum` of the file first, apply the mutation with the Edit tool (never a shell one-liner — backslash and escape collapse through the shell can duplicate or corrupt a guard), confirm the anchor matched exactly once, run only the affected test file, then restore by reversing the Edit and re-check the sha256 equals the pre-drill value (never `git checkout`, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree). D1 REPLACEMENT: change the ACTIVE-present branch from returning CURRENT to DELETE-then-INSERT returning INSTALLED — the restore-preservation test AND the race test must go red on an OUTCOME assertion (the winner's digest/refs and the sorted-outcomes assertion), not on a compile error. D2: delete the PENDING guard — the PENDING_PRESENT cases must go red on the code assertion. D3: delete the history EXISTS check — both history fixtures must go red. D4: delete the rowMatchesBinding cross-check — the diverged-column case must go red. Read each failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets; a red for the wrong reason (a compile error, a hung worker, or every test failing at once) means the drill or the environment is broken, not that the guard is proven. Record the reddened test names and the decisive failure line for the completion evidence.

Close out. Re-measure every production file touched with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line undercounts) and confirm recovery-initial-install.ts is <=250 and sqlite-event-store.ts is under 400. Run the fresh full gate `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store test` from the repo root and keep its verbatim tail as the completion evidence, plus the pass count compared against the ~453-test store baseline so no existing test silently disappeared. Run the adversarial-self-review skill over the whole diff, specifically: what happens if this runs twice concurrently on the same file; what a caller does with CURRENT versus INSTALLED (authority must come only from INSTALLED); whether any refusal constant leaked observed data; whether any guard can be answered by an earlier one and thereby go untested; and whether a poisoned handle can still be mistaken for a benign refusal. Then stage the owned paths explicitly — `git add` is required first for the new untracked files, because a commit pathspec naming an untracked path commits nothing at all — verify `git status --porcelain` shows no foreign path staged (this worktree is shared; .moe/** and packages/runner/** belong to other agents), commit with `git commit -- <the 8 owned paths>`, and confirm with `git show --stat` that only those paths landed. Report the base-ref diff `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD -- packages/store/src` for QA.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Adding the new reason codes to the SHARED RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES registry — REJECTED: recovery-install-entrypoint.test.ts:33 asserts `reasonCodeCount: 8` inside a whole-object toEqual, so four new codes redden an existing test the DoD requires green, and repairing it would pull the entrypoint test + its worker into the owned set (11 distinct files, over the daemon's 10-file bar). A separate narrowly named closed registry also matches task rail 1 ('a separate narrowly named initial-install capability'). (2) Adding a third refusal LAYER — REJECTED: recovery-install.test.ts:77 asserts RECOVERY_INSTALL_LAYERS toEqual exactly two; the two existing layers already carry the distinction the DoD wants. (3) Putting the new method in recovery-install.ts — REJECTED: 191 + ~140 lines busts the 250 target. (4) Returning a plain REFUSED for a pre-existing ACTIVE — REJECTED: refusals here are frozen module constants that may carry no observed data, so a refusal cannot hand back 'the exact valid current winner' the deliverable requires. CURRENT is therefore ok:true with authority NONE plus a stable code+layer, satisfying both the deliverable sentence and DoD 3's 'exact stable code and layer'. (5) Racing two handles in one thread — impossible: node:sqlite is synchronous, so a second BEGIN IMMEDIATE cannot overlap without a worker thread.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD d7a71cb, 2026-08-14. GAP CONFIRMED OPEN: `grep -rn 'installInitialRecoveryBinding|InitialInstall|pristine|PRISTINE' --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs packages/ apps/` returns ZERO hits; positive control `grep -rn 'installRecoveryBinding' packages/store/src` returns 22, so the empty result is a real absence and not a broken grep. Nothing to re-implement, nothing already landed.

CHAIN: SqliteEventStore (sqlite-event-store.ts:93, a frozen facade holding #core) -> createDecisionLedgerCore (decision-ledger.ts:84, frozen delegate object) -> DecisionLedgerStore extends RecoveryInstallStore extends DecisionTransactionStore ... extends StoreRuntime. Inserting RecoveryInitialInstallStore between DecisionLedgerStore and RecoveryInstallStore adds the capability without touching any other layer. A method must be added in FOUR places to be reachable: the class, the DecisionLedgerCore interface, the frozen delegate literal, and the facade.

EXISTING SEMANTICS (do not change): recovery-install.ts:145 writeBindingUnderLock DELETEs the slot then INSERTs — that is the replacement path task rail 1 protects. recovery-install.ts:167 releaseInstallTransaction is the only place that decides poison-vs-clean-rollback; reuse it rather than duplicating. rowMatchesBinding (recovery-install.ts:54) is the row-vs-bytes cross-check that yields RECOVERY_BINDING_ROW_DIVERGED. All are module-private today and need export/protected widening only.

PRISTINE SOURCES: the recovery_bindings table is `slot TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (slot IN ('ACTIVE','PENDING'))` with `incarnation_ref UNIQUE` (sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts). Authoritative history tables are command_decisions (has project_id; two FKs, to command_receipts and domain_events), command_receipts, domain_events (FK -> command_receipts), outbox_messages (FK -> domain_events), aggregate_heads (NO FK). foreign_keys is forced ON and verified =1 at open (sqlite-event-store.ts:203), so in a consistent database command_receipts non-empty is implied by any of decisions/events/outbox — but a foreign writer with FKs off can leave an orphan, which is why all five legs are checked. store_metadata and store_project_binding always carry bootstrap rows and must NOT count as history.

STARTUP VALIDATORS CONSTRAIN THE FIXTURES: validateStartup (decision-ledger.ts:34) runs validateAllReceipts (event-read-materialization.ts:235, which re-materializes every receipt) and validateAllCommandDecisions on EVERY open. A hand-mutilated database that keeps only command_receipts or only domain_events will therefore throw STORE_CORRUPT at open and cannot be used as a fixture. aggregate_heads-only IS openable (both validators scan zero rows) — that is why the history table has exactly two fixtures, one real committed decision covering the mutually-dependent tables jointly and one isolated aggregate_heads row.

RACE HARNESS: command-decision-test-helpers.ts:150 startDecisionRaceWorker + :217 releaseDecisionRace is the two-phase gate pattern (slot 0 releases the open, slot 1 releases the operation) and command-decision-race-worker.mjs is the worker shape; workers run with execArgv ['--experimental-strip-types'] and import .ts specifiers directly. Because the pristine read happens INSIDE BEGIN IMMEDIATE, the loser blocks on the write lock and then observes the winner's row — the race outcome is deterministic ([CURRENT, INSTALLED]), not probabilistic, so this test should not be flaky.

FILE COUNTS (grep -c ''): recovery-install.ts 191, recovery-install-contracts.ts 167, sqlite-event-store.ts 358 (pre-existing, +8 keeps it under the 400 split bar), decision-ledger.ts 146, index.ts 110. Every production .ts has a sibling one-line .js bridge (`export * from './x.ts';`) because intra-package imports use .js specifiers — a new module without its bridge breaks the runtime-loadability tests.

CONSUMER EDGE (epic rail 4 clause 1): this is a store primitive, not a pure package drop. Its named consumer task is task-e19074f841f9450296799abfba9bfcaa (genesis recovery binding in createStoreDependencies), which is BLOCKED pending exactly this capability; task-2846816783104c52bfd4226782b10cc0 and task-69fdb23140ab472ebd34c3e4478c3ef2 are its siblings. No cross-package dependency edge is involved — every owned path is inside @moe/store.

SIZE: 8 steps, 8 distinct files — over the 5-file soft warn, under the 12-step/10-file hard bar. The count is driven by the four-place publication chain plus the mandatory .js bridge and race worker, not by bundled scope.
planningNotes.risks:
1. GUARD MASKING — every refusal case must be built so only the guard under test can answer. A store carrying a PENDING binding usually also carries an ACTIVE one; a store with committed history also has aggregate_heads. Assert the pre-state row counts, and include the both-slots-occupied case that pins PENDING_PRESENT as the first answer.
2. HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER — on Windows an open handle makes afterEach rmSync throw EPERM and the run dies with zero test output, which reads as a native crash. Open and close inside every `it` (and inside the race worker's finally, before postMessage), never in a describe body.
3. CURRENT MUST NOT READ AS AUTHORITY — ok:true with outcome CURRENT is the loser's answer. It carries authority "NONE" and is not INSTALLED; the daemon consumer must gate genesis on outcome === "INSTALLED" alone. Say so in the method comment so the consumer task cannot misread it.
4. THE DECODED BYTES ARE THE AUTHORITY — build the CURRENT winner from decodeRecoveryBinding's output, never from the indexed columns; a row whose columns disagree with its bytes must refuse ROW_DIVERGED, not be reconciled toward either side.
5. UNPROVABLE OUTCOME — a failing COMMIT or a failing ROLLBACK must poison the handle and raise DurableStoreError OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Returning a refusal there would hand genesis a benign-looking answer over durable state nobody can prove.
6. SHARED WORKTREE — .moe/** and packages/runner/** carry other agents' uncommitted work. Never git add -A, never stash (git stash -u deletes peers' untracked files), never reset. A whole-tree commit by the completion hook may capture your bytes into a foreign commit; that is a known hazard, not something to repair — report the base-ref diff instead.
7. DRILL RESTORE — restore each mutation by reversing the Edit and comparing sha256 to the pre-drill value. git checkout would revert to HEAD and destroy uncommitted work; a drill left applied silently poisons every later measurement.
8. EXISTING TESTS ARE EXACT — recovery-install-entrypoint.test.ts pins reasonCodeCount 8, recovery-install.test.ts pins the two-layer array, recovery-anchor.test.ts:593 asserts anchor codes are NOT in RECOVERY_INSTALL_REASON_CODES. Keep the new registry separate and disjoint and all three stay green.
